questions.learningObjective: Apply payment methods and money transfer concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: Think it over: Jasmine Câmara receives $580 of monthly income and spends $29 on childcare. What percentage of income is that?

options.misconception: forgets to multiply the fraction by one hundred
divides the whole by the part instead of the part by the whole
reports the dollar amount rather than the percentage share

questions.explanation: The share is the part divided by the whole, then multiplied by one hundred. $29 divided by $580 is 0.05 as a decimal, so 5% of income goes to childcare. Dividing the other way or skipping the factor of one hundred gives a different, wrong figure.
questions.hint: Divide the expense by income, then convert to a percent.

questions.subject: PERSONAL_FINANCE
questions.learningObjective: Apply payment methods and money transfer concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: Here is the case: Emil Hassan receives a call demanding immediate payment by wire transfer and threatening penalties for delay. What is the safest response?

options.text: Send the payment quickly to avoid the threatened penalties.
options.misconception: lets urgency and fear override verification

options.text: Assume the call is real because the caller sounds authoritative.
options.misconception: uses tone of voice as proof of legitimacy

options.text: Give the caller personal details to confirm the account.
options.misconception: hands sensitive information to an unverified party

options.text: Stop, verify the claim through an independent official channel, and do not wire money.

questions.explanation: Treat an unsolicited demand for immediate wire payment as suspicious, especially when penalties are threatened. Verify independently before acting, and never hand over account details to someone who contacted you unexpectedly.
questions.hint: Urgency plus wire transfer is a warning sign.
